'''Secret Squirrel''' is a sealed deck format in which each player plays the product they open as their deck, without swapping, drafting or a deck construction period. The [[Players Committee]]'s ''Alternate Format Tournament Guide'' (revised September 2015) defines it with one Jabba's Palace Official Tournament Sealed Deck ([[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]]) per player.<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Star Wars CCG Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), Players Committee. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195355/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

* '''Type:''' sealed deck
* '''Defined by:''' Players Committee (Alternate Format Tournament Guide, 2015); played at Decipher's DecipherCon 2002
* '''Card pool:''' one Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck per player; more product may be added
* '''In use:''' by 2002 &ndash; listed in 2015
* '''GEMP:''' none

== Card pool ==
The guide's rules:<ref name="afg" />
* Each player needs one Jabba's Palace Official Tournament Sealed Deck. Additional product may be included.
* Product is not exchanged or drafted, and there is no deck construction period. A deck consists of the product the player opens.
* A player may look through the deck to find any Objectives, starting Locations and Starting Interrupt they wish to use. A player with more than one Objective may include only one.
* Who goes first is decided at random. Both players may play Starting Interrupts of the same name.
* A player who deploys a location chooses whether its Light Side or Dark Side game text faces them.
* A player may deploy a unique Effect even if the opponent has a copy in play, may not persona replace the opponent's characters, and may convert their own location.

An optional rule set: the Light Side objective is randomly assigned to one player and the Dark Side objective to the other; all ability 1 characters are considered ability 2; and [[Lando With Vibro-Ax]], [[The Camp]] and [[His Name Is Anakin]] are banned.<ref name="afg" />

In a Secret Squirrel event the Final Confrontation pairs the top two players, not the top Light and top Dark players.<ref name="afg" /> Sealed games are timed at one minute per card in the deck.<ref name="afg" />

== History ==
[[DecipherCon 2002]]'s Star Wars schedule listed two "Secret Squirrel" sealed events of 4 games, on 31 October and 3 November 2002, and its Young Jedi schedule had a Secret Squirrel sealed event too.<ref name="swsched">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/events/eventschedule-otherccg.html Event schedule: Star Wars, Young Jedi, Jedi Knights], DecipherCon 2002, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021023190505/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/events/eventschedule-otherccg.html Internet Archive].</ref> The schedule does not say what product those events used. At the [[2007 World Championship]], [[Patrick Johnson|Pat Johnson]] said he had won a Secret Squirrel tournament at Origins 2006.<ref name="yt-swSmLNAG62A">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=swSmLNAG62A Worlds 2007 P Johnson Interview], Star Wars CCG channel, YouTube (7 April 2026). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015174617/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=swSmLNAG62A Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[2007 World Championship interviews (transcript)]].</ref>

The name was also used for Cube play. The Players Committee's 2013 Game Formats page described a "Squirrel format" for the Cube, in which all cards of both sides are shuffled together and drafted in one pod.<ref name="pc-gameformats">[http://www.starwarsccg.org/about/game-formats/ Game Formats], Players Committee. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20131213093344/http://www.starwarsccg.org/about/game-formats/ Internet Archive].</ref> The 2015 guide calls this the "Secret Squirrel" type of Watto's Cube event.<ref name="afg" /> See [[Cube]].
